I've been doing content for about 2 years. 1 year in Davinci. I will say it is an absolute headache at first. It is daunting to anyone new to the editing world, believe me. I've been there myself. But don't give up because its hard. Form the idea of what you want to make in your head, even jot down some notes if it helps you remember what you envisioned. If you don't know how to create the effects you want, there's a few really good channels out there that run a step by step guide.

If you're doing this as content creation, I, as well as many other YouTubers, find that the simpler your videos are, the better they do. Remember, you're not making a high end studio movie so don't make a million edits if you don't have to. Put some smooth transitions in there, maybe an intro and outro. Some light audio work IF it needs it, but ultimately dialing in tour audio settings in the recording process generally suffices unless you want to add audio effects.

And don't forget, experience comes with time and skill comes with repetition. You give up, you lose everything you learn. Eventually you'll be able to create something that is absolutely awesome and you'll be proud of yourself for it. You got this!

@21:00 I respect the editing and the process so this is ENTIRELY preference

John Ghibli (I forgot the Studio Ghibli guy's name) once mentioned a concept called "Ma". Which is essentially empty space, or breathing room.

And here you're literally like... there's a breath here, let's cut that out.

I sincerely wonder what the benefit is, and if it offsets the cost.

Something about the emptiness, the breathing room, seeing a creator rush to cattails and say "ooo, cattails", adds a narrative context that's more organic to me. Without that organic narrative context, I often forget the name of a creator.

Seeing a person go "ooo, cattails" and collect some cattails, means just a little bit more if you watch them actually run to the cattails. Even before that, is when they didn't see the cattails to begin with. Watching excitement exist is... fine? But watching it come into being is something else. Humans live in full breaths, not just exclamations. A full cup doesn't tell as much of a story as a cup being filled. And that's what Ma does, I think; it contrasts something with nothingness.


I fully believe this is an intentional and rational decision, to cut out these bits of Ma. So I guess I'm just thinking out loud about the cost and benefit.

I also think I'm reading too much into it all. I think I wouldn't watch this kind of content, but I probably do and don't even realize how much is being cut out.

3 months ago (edited)
Rough cuts at 2X speed is a really great time saver. Since you don't have to focus on exactly what is said, you can even go to 4X, once you get comfy with it.
Then using a combo of Slice ("Ctrl + B") and Trim Start ("Ctrl + Shift + [") and Trim End ("Ctrl + Shift + ]") you can quickly gut the footage down to just the usable parts.

I don't like using markers, because they seem to be hit and miss. Sometimes when I cut content, the markers slide. Sometimes they don't. And I have no idea what governs that behaviour. So I just cut directly. The cut will be a pretty obvious marker anyway.

I use the markers for other things instead, like when I've cut the footage down and wanna give myself placeholders for B-roll or remind myself of a cool transition I thought of for that particular cut or things like that, so I can focus the first run on cutting, the second run on B-roll, third on transitions and, if necessary, the fourth on censoring.

I feel like Proxy Media is useful, but shouldn't be used for the entire media pool like that.
Why take up all that extra space, if you don't need it? Just cut out the parts where your computer struggle, and use proxies on just those parts, it'll save you a LOT of space.

I'm running on a pre-COVID laptop without a dedicated graphics card, and Resolve runs just fine with source quality clips, even 5-8 hour long clips.
I got resources to spare in every department except for storage space, so adding an 8 hour long proxy because that one glitch transition lagged a little in the preview seems like a lot of waste.

I to mark in, O to mark out, right-click and select Create Sub-clip. Now you can proxy just the bit you need!

It wasn't explained in the video, but the use cases for Cut Start and Cut End are quite different. 
It mainly depends on if you're editing from the start, knowing what you want to cut. For scripted content, Cut Start will probably be what you'll use the most, like shown in this video.

That saves you from having to find the end of the last highlight and the start of this one, just one cut and you're there.
